findings.what: All fifteen files in evidence/.previous/ are byte-identical to this capture's artifacts of the same name (md5 of 01_pulse.png 7f875803c98c on both sides; the same for all ten stills and all five clips), and .previous/CAPTURED_AT reads 2026-09-09T05:28:27 while DIFF.json declares its baseline captured at 2026-09-09T03:37:07 — the baseline was rolled forward onto this capture after the diff was written and before the critics read it.
findings.why: The row asks this critic to judge each artifact against its evidence/.previous/ counterpart; with eleven artifacts labelled `changed` and every previous_sha unreachable, that half of the report cannot be grounded in a before-and-after, and DIFF.json's own SSIM numbers cannot be checked against the files.

findings.where: the whole artifact set: MANIFEST.json browser "webkit", reception.json browser "chromium"
findings.what: Both absent artifacts (09_two_devices.png, 16_setup_android.png) are the only two that would have been photographed on Android, so every one of the fifteen delivered artifacts, both crop scenes and all fifty-eight logs come from the PWA under WebKit or, for reception, Chromium; there is no picture of the Android build anywhere in the evidence.
findings.why: The row's fourth clause — both platforms serve the same regions, the same feelings and the same event types from the one codebase — has zero artifact evidence; I judge the stated reason a reason and not an excuse (no /dev/kvm, adbd answering only after 113 minutes with no framework behind it, no GTK, nothing faked from the PWA) and the code half checks out, but the clause is unphotographed and this critic can only half-verify it.

findings.where: the four result cards from y=1150 to the fold, under the PHOTOGRAPHS facet
findings.what: The record says type_filter "photographs", hits 6, kinds {photo: 6}, and not one of the six is shown as a photograph: every hit is a line of ink on paper reading "noor sent a photograph — …" with the matched word in highlighter and no thumbnail (confirmed in app/lib/regions/chat/search_page.dart, where _Hit renders summaryOf(e) plus a timestamp and has no branch for a blob at all).
findings.why: The same photo event is a print in Chat and a print in Moments and loses its picture entirely in Search, so an event's identity is not consistent across the views onto the one log — and the facet whose whole purpose is finding photographs is the one that shows none.

findings.where: the to-do row at y 960-1030, against 11_chat_scroll.mp4 frame 294 (app time 4.70 s)
findings.what: The same event type is marked two different ways: on the Us desk an open item carries a hand-drawn cross ("× tape the gap in the back room window  noor"), while the same kind of item in the thread carries an empty pencil box ("☐ the pressure at hers again, and find out why it keeps dropping / back on the list").
findings.why: A cross conventionally reads as struck off and an empty box as still open, so one to-do event reads as two opposite states depending on which region it is seen in — the row wants the same event to appear consistently wherever it appears.

findings.where: the lens row at rows 300-370 against the filter chips at rows 390-480
findings.what: The three lenses (WHAT WE SENT / WHAT HAPPENED / WHAT WE FELT) are stamped straight onto the wood — 5.7 per cent of that band is paper by area — while the person and range chips twenty pixels below sit on paper at 47.4 per cent, and every other selector in the app (the five tabs, the fifteen search facets, the six family tabs in the picker) is an index card.
findings.why: It is the one switch in the five regions that is not a piece of paper, so the single most repeated element of the visual language breaks in the middle of one screen, and the selected lens is carried only by an underline.

findings.where: the partner strip, frames 0-410 against frames 411-517
findings.what: The partner's place changes as a word (TRAVELLING → OUT) but the mood change that happens in the same frame is carried only by a paper swap: a clean 140x65 patch of the strip moves from mean 189.0 to 195.8 and R/B 1.277 to 1.294 at frame 411 (app time 6.58 s), because assignment.dart:59-67 sends bright to legal and restless to sticky_yellow, and both are yellow.
findings.why: Mood is the headline declared signal and the strip is the only place partner state is legible on every screen, so the most important thing it carries is the least readable thing on it — a 7-grey-level change a person would read as the same sheet of paper.

findings.what: The record names six ids in `view.order` (all photos, the hits the page is showing) and six different ids in `visible` (0001M3AY…, 0001M4GW… and four others, which are the feeling and state rows of the chat thread underneath the sheet).

what_is_working: One log, and the records say the same number from five different rooms: 01_pulse, 02_chat, 03_us, 04_moments and 05_settings all report events 14062, sync.cursor 14062 and the identical ambient standing line "bright · week one, and the room smells right again · travelling · 7 hours ago".

The Moments lens counts are exactly the registry's `lens` field summed: media 183 = photo 115 + video 14 + voice_note 54 (04_moments.report.json), and milestones 154 = date_event 81 + milestone 6 + ritual_kept 53 + passed_on 12 + feeling_authored 2 (03_us.report.json), with todo_event — the one type that declares no lens — correctly absent from both.

No second store: one SpineStore interface with three drivers (memory, sqlite3, IndexedDB) all under lib/spine/store/, and test/persistence_boundary_test.dart fails the build on any storage-driver import outside lib/spine/. The service worker keeps no per-type table of its own — reception.json shows 18 preference rows for the registry's 18 types and words_for_kinds 14, exactly the 14 types that declare a `pushed` line, the other four being the four whose notify is `none`.

The fifth-module cost is one line, counted rather than taken on trust: my own grep for each of the five modules' id, event type and renderer id ('dates'/'date_event'/'ticket_stub' and the twelve others) across every .dart under lib/ and every .js, .json and .html under web/ returns zero files outside lib/modules/<id>/ and lib/spine/types.dart.

05_settings.png reads the registry aloud: the nine interrupt rows on the glass are, in order, 'something written', 'a picture', 'something to watch', 'their voice', 'an answer to something of yours', 'a feeling', 'something they say about themselves', 'something their phone notices', 'a date moving' — the `announced` strings of message, photo, video, voice_note, reaction, feeling, state_declared, state_passive, date_event in registry order, and their wake me/quietly settings match reception.json's by_type exactly.

One shell over five regions, measured: the partner strip occupies rows 0-281 of 3120 and is pixel-identical across 01_pulse, 03_us, 04_moments, 05_settings and 12_search (max 5 grey levels, mean 0.05), and identical in 02_chat and 13_messenger_states apart from the note edge intruding at rows 282-290. The feeling corner is a 75x75 lifted page corner at x 1365-1439, y 2868-2942, present and identical to within a mean of 0.21 grey levels in all nine non-modal stills including 10_first_run and 17_setup_pwa. The same five-card tab strip is in all nine.

The state slot degrades into the same slot rather than disappearing: in 10_first_run and 17_setup_pwa the strip is replaced by 'nothing from them yet. the six words are on the other phone.' in the same place, and those two bands are identical to each other to within 1 grey level.

The same event carries the same object between regions: the pink 'nyeh' sweet on Pulse's shelf (01_pulse.png, x 960-1180, y 1220-1400) is the same rendered object stuck to the bottom-right of the 15:14 note in 02_chat.png, which is the one reaction 02_chat.report.json records, on target 00015WD17011152HXP55ZPFPYA — the second of the eight ids, whose stock lined_03 matches the white ruled sheet it is on.

A shared-life module's event is a row in the one thread, not a feed of its own: 11_chat_scroll.mp4 frame 294 shows a to-do drawn with the todos module's own pencil-box body, its action written underneath ('back on the list'), and the same 'read ✓✓' marks a message carries.

A feeling the couple made is not special-cased anywhere: haptics.check.json counts 36 feelings, 34 built-in and 2 authored, sorted into the same six families with no separate bucket; crops/haptics_strip.png lists 'pigeon' (mischief) and 'tuesday soup' (shelter) in the same table on the same 3500 ms scale; and 15_authored_feeling.mp4 shows 'pigeon' in the mischief grid beside six built-ins at frame 60, landing on the Us desk at frame 120, and on Pulse's shelf between 'tuesday soup' and 'nuzzle' at frame 180.

Search reaches the shared-life modules from the module registry rather than a hand-written list: 12_search.png's facet row carries DATES, TO DO, DATES THAT MATTER, RITUALS and THE SHELF alongside WRITTEN, PHOTOGRAPHS, VIDEO, TALKING, FEELINGS and STATE, which is search_page.dart's `for (final m in kModules) m.label: m.eventTypes`; reliability.json's search check answers nine queries each with an event of the type asked about, todo_event, date_event and milestone among them.

Neither platform's code knows the domain: the whole Android layer is 270 lines of Kotlin (MainActivity 12, Widget 55, Haptics 68, Ambient 135) and names no region, module, event type or feeling — only the three channels io.lovetap/ambient, lovetap/haptics and the widget — while the five regions are one IndexedStack in app/lib/app.dart with no platform branch anywhere near it.

The material language survives the second lighting condition: crops/dusk_pulse.png is the same layout with the same components at mean luma 137.4 against 164.5 in day, the six shelf objects re-lit rather than recoloured, and hairline.json finds 0 mask-edge rules in all ten stills.

verdict: On the four clauses of the row, three hold under measurements I took myself rather than on the code's own say-so. There is one log: five region records taken minutes apart all report events 14062 and cursor 14062 and the same standing line, and Moments' lens counts are the registry's `lens` field summed exactly — media 183 = 115 photos + 14 videos + 54 voice notes, happened 154 = 81 + 6 + 53 + 12 + 2 — with the one type that declares no lens correctly missing from both. There is no second store: one SpineStore behind three drivers all under lib/spine/store/, a test that fails the build on a driver import anywhere else, and a service worker that keeps no per-type table of its own, which reception.json proves numerically with 18 preference rows for 18 registry types and 14 push words for the 14 types that declare one. A fifth module really is a directory and a line: my own grep for all fifteen module handles across every Dart file in lib/ and every JS, JSON and HTML file in web/ finds nothing outside the modules' own directories and the spine registry. And the artifacts show one system rather than an assembly — the partner strip is pixel-identical across five regions and the search sheet, the feeling corner is the same 75x75 lifted corner in all nine non-modal stills including first run, a to-do turns up as a row of the chat thread with the same read ticks a message carries, and the couple's own 'pigeon' sits in the picker beside the built-ins, lands on the Us desk and appears on Pulse's shelf without a badge anywhere saying it was made here. The point comes off for the fourth clause and for the small change: not one artifact was taken on Android, so 'both platforms serve the same regions, the same feelings and the same event types' rests entirely on my reading of 270 lines of Kotlin that name no region, module, type or feeling — an honest, measured absence, but an absence; and four cross-region details still disagree with each other, of which the sharpest is that a photograph found by the search facet built for photographs is shown as a line of text. Separately and seriously: evidence/.previous/ has been rolled forward onto this capture — all fifteen files match by md5 and its CAPTURED_AT is two hours later than the baseline time DIFF.json declares — so every `changed` label in DIFF.json is unverifiable and the judgements above are judgements of the current files, not comparisons.
